issues.t: Front lower ball joint wear and separation (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, steering that wanders, uneven wear on the inner edge of the front tires, and in the worst case a front wheel that suddenly folds under the truck.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints on these trucks can wear out far too early. Toyota recalled 2002-2004 trucks because the ball surface could be scratched at the factory, and 2004-2007 trucks because the grease inside could break down. Some aftermarket replacement joints were also recalled for being too soft.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer run your VIN for the ball joint recalls. If you hear clunking or the steering feels loose, get the front end inspected before driving at speed, because a separated joint can cause a loss of control.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs at all. The danger only shows up in a crash, when the passenger front airbag deploys.
issues.why: These trucks used Takata passenger airbag inflators whose propellant breaks down after years of heat and humidity. In a crash the inflator can burst and throw metal fragments into the cabin. Some inflators that were already replaced once were recalled again.
issues.next: Check your VIN on NHTSA's recall site or with a Toyota dealer today. The replacement is free, and until it is done nobody should ride in the front passenger seat.

issues.t: Frame rust (frame replacement program)
issues.sym: Rust scaling, flaking or perforation on the frame rails and crossmembers, usually worst in snowy states that salt the roads.
issues.why: Some frames from these years did not have enough rust protection. Toyota ran corrosion-protection and frame replacement programs, and a class action settlement covered inspections, rust-proofing and frame replacement for 2005-2008 Sequoias.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected promptly. Ask a Toyota dealer whether your VIN was covered by the frame or corrosion-proofing programs, and do not tow with a badly rusted frame.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the engine on a cold start that often fades as it warms up. You may also smell exhaust or see a check engine light.
issues.why: The cast iron exhaust manifolds on the 4.7L V8 crack after years of heating and cooling, most often on the driver's side. Exhaust then leaks out of the crack before it reaches the rest of the exhaust.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the leak. A quick check is soapy water sprayed on a cold manifold while the engine starts. Fix it before fumes get into the cabin or the leak throws off the oxygen sensors.

issues.t: Oxygen sensor heater failures
issues.sym: Check engine light, often with code P0051 or a similar oxygen sensor heater code. Some owners also notice rough idle or lower fuel economy.
issues.why: The heater circuit inside the oxygen sensors burns out. Early Sequoias are known for repeat oxygen sensor failures.
issues.next: Have the code read to see which sensor is at fault, then replace that sensor. Lean codes like P0171 or P0174 point to a different problem and should be diagnosed separately.

issues.t: Secondary air injection pump or valve failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes in the P2440-P2445 range, a loud buzz or whine right after a cold start, and sometimes a rough cold idle or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: The air pump and its switching valves blow fresh air into the exhaust for a minute or two after a cold start. Water can get inside them, and they rust until the pump seizes or a valve sticks. Toyota issued a bulletin on water getting into the pumps and extended coverage on these parts for some years.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pump and valves tested. Ask a Toyota dealer whether any extended coverage applies to your VIN before paying for parts.

issues.t: ABS and VSC lights from a faulty yaw rate sensor
issues.sym: The ABS and VSC (stability control) warning lights come on together, sometimes flashing, often with codes C1223 and C1244.
issues.why: A sensor under the center console that measures how the truck is turning or slowing can fail or be knocked out of position by a bent bracket. With bad readings, the system shuts off ABS and stability control.
issues.next: Have the brake system codes read. Normal braking still works, but ABS and stability control may be off until the sensor is replaced or its mounting fixed.

issues.t: Stability control can kick in at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: When pulling away or accelerating at low speed, the stability control engages briefly on its own and the truck feels like it is holding back.
issues.why: On some 2003 Sequoias the skid control computer did not store the steering angle sensor's center position correctly, so it thought the truck was sliding when it was not.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check your VIN for this recall. The fix is a free reprogramming.

issues.t: Front brakes wearing out early
issues.sym: Front pads wear out much faster than expected, often with grinding, squealing, uneven pad wear or a pull when braking.
issues.why: The Sequoia is very heavy for its front brakes. In salty areas the caliper slide pins can also rust and seize, so the pads drag and wear unevenly.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked at every tire rotation. When replacing pads, make sure the slide pins are cleaned and greased or replaced.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may deploy on their own (recall)
issues.sym: No warning beforehand. The side curtain airbags can go off when the truck has not crashed, for example while off-roading or on a rough road.
issues.why: The airbag control module on trucks with roll-sensing curtain airbags could be programmed in a way that triggers deployment when it should not.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-065 and have the free fix done.

issues.t: Seat heater wiring can short and burn (recall)
issues.sym: A heated seat that stops working, gets very hot in one spot, or a burning smell from the seat.
issues.why: Repeated sitting and getting in and out can damage the seat heater wiring in the cushion until it shorts. Some dealer-installed aftermarket seat heaters had the same risk and were recalled separately.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater if it smells or overheats. Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN for the seat heater recalls.

issues.t: Leaking water pump
issues.sym: Pink crusty residue around the water pump, low coolant, a whine or grinding from the front of the engine that rises with engine speed, or the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: The water pump bearing wears out and the seal behind it starts leaking coolant out of the weep hole. Toyota published a bulletin on inspecting these pumps for leaks.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and replace a leaking or noisy pump before the engine overheats. Make sure the leak is not actually coming from the timing cover above it.

issues.t: Power steering gear can leak and lose assist (recall)
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid dripping under the front, a low power steering reservoir, a whine when turning, or steering that suddenly becomes very heavy.
issues.why: Some power steering gear assemblies were built in a way that lets oil leak out. If enough fluid is lost, the power assist can drop out without warning. Some replacement gears sold as parts were also recalled.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 21V-920 and 21E-103. Do not let the reservoir run dry, and have any leak looked at soon.

issues.t: Sticking accelerator pedal (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels stiff, is slow to come back up, or stays partly pressed when you let off.
issues.why: Wear and moisture inside the pedal assembly can increase friction on a lever in the pedal, so it does not return smoothly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V-017. If the pedal sticks while driving, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and pull over.

issues.t: Driver's power window switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Windows that work only some of the time, a burning smell or melted look at the driver's window switch, or smoke from the door panel.
issues.why: The grease on the master window switch contacts was applied unevenly at the factory. Dirt and moisture can then cause a short that overheats the switch.
issues.next: Stop using the switch if you smell burning. Check your VIN for recalls 12V-491 and 15V-689 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, hard starting, or the engine cutting out while driving and not restarting.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank can stop working properly and cut fuel to the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 20V-012 and 20V-682 and have the pump replaced for free. A stall in traffic is dangerous, so do not wait.

issues.t: Airbags may not deploy after a false fault (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on at startup. On 2018 trucks the stability control light may also come on.
issues.why: Electrical noise could make the airbag computer think it had a fault, which could stop the airbags from deploying in a crash. On some 2018 trucks the same noise could also turn off stability control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 18V-685 and 18V-122. The fix is a free software update at a Toyota dealer.

issues.t: Twin-turbo V6 engine failure reports
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, a sudden loss of power, or an engine that stops and will not restart. Some owners have reported the engine seizing.
issues.why: The same twin-turbo V6 family in the non-hybrid Tundra and Lexus LX 600 was recalled for machining debris left in the engine that can damage the bearings. The hybrid Sequoia has not been part of that recall, but a small number of owners have reported engine failures.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and change it on time. If you hear knocking or lose power, stop and have the SUV towed to a Toyota dealer, since the engine is covered by Toyota's powertrain warranty for the first years.

issues.t: Hybrid system malfunction warning with loss of power
issues.sym: A 'Hybrid System Malfunction' warning on the dash, a sudden jerk, and the SUV not accelerating normally.
issues.why: The cause has not been pinned down publicly. Owners of 2023 and 2024 models have reported it, and no recall has been issued so far.
issues.next: Pull over safely, then have a Toyota dealer read the stored codes while they are fresh. Ask about any software updates for the hybrid system.

issues.t: SUV can creep forward in Neutral (recall)
issues.sym: With the shifter in Neutral on flat ground and no foot on the brake, the SUV slowly rolls forward at a few miles per hour.
issues.why: Clutches inside the 10-speed automatic may not fully let go in Neutral, so some power still reaches the wheels.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-125. Until the free software update is done, use Park and the parking brake when stopped instead of Neutral.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the center screen shows a black or green screen, half a green screen, or a frozen picture instead of the camera view.
issues.why: Electrical noise in the video signal to the multimedia screen can scramble the camera data so the picture does not display.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-657 and have the free software update done. Until then, check mirrors and look over your shoulder when backing up.

issues.t: Tow hitch cover can fall off (recall)
issues.sym: The plastic cover over the hitch opening in the rear bumper rattles, works loose, or is missing.
issues.why: The clips that hold the cover in the bumper do not lock in securely, so it can shake loose while driving and become a hazard for drivers behind you.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-640. The dealer installs an improved cover and modifies the bumper for free.

issues.t: Spare tire can drop from its carrier (recall)
issues.sym: A rattle or dragging sound from under the rear, or a spare tire hanging down or missing.
issues.why: A link in the steel chain that holds the spare tire under the vehicle may not have been welded properly and can break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-468. The dealer replaces the spare tire carrier for free.

issues.t: Tires may have sidewall damage (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing obvious from the driver's seat. You might see a bulge or cut on the inside sidewall of a passenger-side tire, or feel a vibration.
issues.why: Some passenger-side tires could have damage on the inner sidewall, which can lead to a sudden air loss.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-767 and have the tires inspected and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Load capacity label may show the wrong weight (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The sticker in the door jamb that tells you how much weight you can carry may list the wrong numbers.
issues.why: The label added for dealer-installed accessories may not show the correct added weight, which could lead an owner to overload the SUV.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-179. The dealer replaces the label for free. Until then, avoid loading the SUV close to its limit.
